title: Online Resource Allocation With General Constraints
claim: Standard dual methods stop violating once the multiplier grows large under budget constraints, but under general constraints violations can persist despite a large multiplier.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, shared legend below, dashed threshold line with annotations
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the same axes: time t on the x-axis and the dual-variable norm ||λ_t||_1 on the y-axis. Each plots a blue trajectory with dots at each round. The left panel is titled 'Budget constraints'. The trajectory rises, crosses a dashed teal threshold at 2/ρ labeled 'large ||λ_t||_1', then bends downward to a green dot labeled 'stop violating'. The right panel is titled 'General constraints'. It follows the same early path but keeps climbing past a dashed maroon 2/ρ line, with red dots throughout and the annotation 'can still violate'. A legend at the bottom explains the blue trajectory line, red violating rounds and green non-violating rounds. Red against green is the main contrast, and the eye goes to the diverging endpoints.
caption: Illustration of the behavior of standard dual algorithms that do not use a weakly adaptive regret minimizers. Left: in the budget-constrained setting, once $\|\bm{\lambda}_t\|_1$ becomes sufficiently large, the algorithm stops violating, and the dual variable starts decreasing. Right: under general constraints, violations may persist even when $\|\bm{\lambda}_t\|_1$ is already large.
abstract: Online resource allocation (ORA) is a fundamental framework for sequential decision-making problems under budget constraints, with applications ranging from online advertising to revenue management. In this work, we study a broader setting that includes both budget constraints and general constraints, extending the classical budget-only model. This extension is essential for modeling critical economic requirements, such as Return-on-Investment (ROI) constraints. We develop an algorithm that achieves best-of-both-world guarantees within this generalized framework. In particular, against a dynamic benchmark, our algorithm achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret in the \emph{stochastic} regime and $Î±$-regret of order $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt{T})$ in the \emph{adversarial} regime, where $Î±$ depends on the feasibility margin of the corresponding offline problem. At the same time, our algorithm guarantees strict satisfaction of the budget constraints and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt{T})$ cumulative violation for the general ones. From a technical perspective, introducing general constraints alongside budgets precludes the use of standard budget-focus methods. While budget methods rely on a zero-consumption ``safe'' action to ensure feasibility, general constraints are much less ``aligned'' towards feasibility. We overcome these difficulties with a new analysis that exploits \emph{weak adaptivity} to get boundedness of the Lagrangian multipliers and best-of-both-world guarantees.
